Maintenance Report — MNT-0055-006

Asset: WELL-0055 (SW-24 Well 055, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 21 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 22 Jul 2023 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 27 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0055-0040 on 2023-07-20 Report written: 24 Jul 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0055-0040 at 08:45 on 2023-07-20 found crude oil on the pad: about 5.9% of the pad area, estimated 1.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 8.2 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 309 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 247 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.1 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0055-006 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.54% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Parts and cost

Absorbents and berms708

Labour (company crew and contractor)1,825
Total5,365

Maintenance Report — MNT-0055-011

Asset: WELL-0055 (SW-24 Well 055, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 28 Apr 2024 08:00 · Finished: 01 May 2024 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 82 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0055-0080 on 2024-04-25 Report written: 03 May 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0055-0080 showed the wellhead at 22.6 °C with the air at 22.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 1 day longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 6 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0055-022

Asset: WELL-0055 (SW-24 Well 055, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 07 Nov 2025 08:00 · Finished: 01 Dec 2025 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 591 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0055-0157 on 2025-11-06 Report written: 02 Dec 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0055-0157 showed the wellhead at 15.9 °C with the air at 16.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 23 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0055-022 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0055-026

Asset: WELL-0055 (SW-24 Well 055, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 03 May 2026 08:00 · Finished: 12 May 2026 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 227 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0055-0180 on 2026-04-30 Report written: 14 May 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0055-0180 showed the wellhead at 26.8 °C with the air at 25.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 7 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Saddle bearing assembly1,892
Bolts, shims and seals473
Bearing grease and consumables789
Labour (company crew)1,455
Total4,609

Compliance check

Manual §10Action required3 corrective repairs on this equipment in 12 months; root-cause analysis to be started

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
  • Start a root-cause analysis for this equipment before the next repair is closed (well-type manual, section 10).
